title: Sikhism: rising spirits
hook: Sikhs speak of staying in high spirits, even in hard times

segments.voice: Yesterday: langar, the free kitchen where everyone eats at the same level. Your line was everyone sits together.

You ask someone how they're doing. Their week has been rough, and you know it: a lost job, a sick parent, a flood in the basement. They smile and say something that isn't denial and isn't a brave act either. Something like: it's hard, and we're in good spirits. You can hear they mean both halves. Sikhs have a phrase for that second half, chardi kala, and it isn't a mood you wait for. It's a way of standing.
screen: `HOW ARE YOU DOING?` → `IT'S HARD, AND WE'RE IN GOOD SPIRITS.` → `CHARDI KALA.`

segments.voice: Chardi kala is Punjabi. Chardi means rising, climbing, going up. Kala is harder to put in one English word: spirit, energy, strength, a state of being. Together: rising spirits, or ever-ascending spirit. You'll hear it in ordinary talk, on banners, at the end of messages. And it comes in the Ardas, the prayer Sikhs say standing, near the close of worship. Near its end comes a line that runs, roughly: Nanak, through the Name may our spirits rise, and by your will may there be good for all. Notice the pairing: rising spirits, and the good of everyone. Not just my spirits. It matters that Sikhs, of all people, say this. The Ardas also remembers hard history: Gurus and ordinary Sikhs who were imprisoned, tortured and killed rather than give up their faith. Guru Arjan, the fifth Guru, was executed in Lahore. Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth, was beheaded in Delhi. So chardi kala was never a slogan for easy days. It was learned in the worst ones. And it isn't pretending. Those who speak of it say grief and anger are real; chardi kala is where you stand while you feel them. It rests on trust in the Creator's will, which Sikhs call hukam, and on remembering the Name, the practice from four days ago. The spirit rises because it's tied to something that doesn't sink. For anyone on any path, it offers a question for a bad day: not how do I feel nothing, but where do I stand?
screen: `CHARDI — RISING. KALA — SPIRIT.` · `SAID DAILY IN THE ARDAS.` · `LEARNED IN THE HARDEST DAYS.` · `NOT PRETENDING, STANDING.` · then, large: `RISING SPIRITS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one setback that's with you this week, small or large, and let it be as heavy as it is. On the next breath in, feel your spine lengthen a little, as if something lifts from the crown of your head. The weight is still there; you're just standing a bit taller under it.
Chardi kala. Rising spirits: steady, hopeful strength that holds even in hard times, rooted in trust. Today's word.
Your line: rising spirits. Hard days are real, and so is where you stand. See you tomorrow.
